ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

An irregular pulse in a healthy student

A healthy 19-year-old has an irregular pulse during a routine examination. ECG shows identical upright P waves before every narrow QRS and a stable PR interval. The R-R interval shortens during inspiration and lengthens during expiration. He has no symptoms. Which diagnosis best fits?

  1. Respiratory sinus arrhythmia
  2. Atrial fibrillation
  3. Mobitz type I AV block
  4. Premature atrial contractions
  5. Complete heart block
Answer and explanation

Respiratory sinus arrhythmia

Sinus activation is preserved while the cycle length varies with breathing, a common physiologic pattern in young people.

Option explanations

Respiratory sinus arrhythmia: Sinus activation is preserved while the cycle length varies with breathing, a common physiologic pattern in young people.

Atrial fibrillation: Consistent sinus P waves and respiratory-linked variation argue against atrial fibrillation.

Mobitz type I AV block: Wenckebach would show progressive PR prolongation and a dropped QRS.

Premature atrial contractions: PACs are premature beats, often with altered P-wave morphology, rather than a smooth breathing-linked pattern.

Complete heart block: Complete block produces AV dissociation, not consistent conduction of every sinus P wave.
